rules.when: Well-specified mechanical work whose specification is already precise: a rote rename, a formatting sweep, tests against existing behaviour, documentation generated from a diff, or several such tasks dispatched at once.
rules.why: Sonnet is fast and good value when the task leaves little to judgment, and a wide burst of workers spends less of the subscription window on it.

rules.when: High-leverage planning, architecture, strategy or approach selection, where the worker produces judgment rather than code.
rules.why: Spend the deepest reasoning only where a wrong direction costs the most; use this rule sparingly.
